extra.message: User input from request.GET['host'] is concatenated directly into an OS command string passed to os.system(). An attacker can inject arbitrary shell commands via the 'host' parameter, e.g., 'host=127.0.0.1; cat /etc/passwd'.

User-controlled data from request.body or request.GET['blob'] is passed to pickle.loads(), enabling arbitrary code execution. An attacker can craft a malicious pickle payload that executes arbitrary Python code on the server.

User input from request.GET['fragment'] is concatenated directly into a Jinja2 Template string and rendered as HTML. This allows Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI) leading to remote code execution (e.g., {{ ''.__class__.__mro__[1].__subclasses__() }}) and also XSS since the result is returned as text/html.

An XML parser is created with load_dtd=True, resolve_entities=True, and no_network=False, then used to parse user-controlled request.body. This allows XML External Entity (XXE) attacks to read arbitrary server files or make network requests.

cwe: CWE-611: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference

extra.message: The Notification.url field (CharField, not URLField) is rendered in an href attribute without scheme validation. Django auto-escaping does not neutralize javascript: URLs because they contain no HTML special characters. An attacker who can set a Notification's url field (e.g., via Django admin) can inject javascript: URLs that execute when clicked.

User input from request.GET['lane'] or request.POST['lane'] is passed directly to Django's redirect() without validation. An attacker can craft a URL like /ops/after/course-lane-151/?lane=https://evil.com to redirect users to malicious sites for phishing.

The Origin request header value is reflected back as Access-Control-Allow-Origin with Access-Control-Allow-Credentials set to true. This allows any origin to make authenticated cross-origin requests, bypassing the same-origin policy entirely.

The course_roster_fold_036 view has no authentication check (_wrk_gate) and no @login_required decorator. It returns operational data including a memo about 'renewal risk, payment flags, owner contact details' to any unauthenticated requester.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: The course_identity_ping_338 view has no authentication check (_wrk_gate) and no @login_required decorator. It accepts and reflects back user-controlled 'handle' and 'channel' parameters without any verification, accessible to any unauthenticated requester.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: User-controlled JSON from request.body is parsed and passed to workset.update(payload), allowing the attacker to override any key in the dictionary including 'role', 'tier', 'approved', and 'balance'. There is no allowlist of permitted keys.

cwe: CWE-915: Improperly Controlled Modification of Dynamically-Determined Object Attributes

extra.message: The random.choice() function from Python's random module (which is not cryptographically secure) is used to generate what appears to be a nonce or token code. An attacker can predict the output if they can infer the random state. The secrets module should be used instead.

cwe: CWE-338: Use of Cryptographically Weak Pseudo-Random Number Generator

extra.message: ssl._create_unverified_context() is used to create an SSL context that disables certificate verification for an outbound HTTPS request. This makes the connection vulnerable to man-in-the-middle attacks.

The response explicitly sets X-XSS-Protection to '0' and clears the Content-Security-Policy header, disabling browser-level XSS protections. This weakens the defense-in-depth posture of the application.
MD5 hashing is used to digest user-supplied input. MD5 is cryptographically broken and unsuitable for security-sensitive purposes such as integrity verification or password hashing.
Server environment details including DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE and the BASE_EXPORT_DIR filesystem path are exposed in the JSON response, providing reconnaissance information to attackers.
The full request body and the Authorization header value are logged at WARNING level, potentially exposing sensitive credentials and PII in application logs.

cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File

extra.message: Hardcoded verifier values {'north': '4812', 'south': '5930'} are used for authentication in course_identity_hint_457. These cannot be rotated without code changes and are visible in source code.

Authorization is determined by a user-controlled cookie (ops_badge) or header (x-ops-badge) compared against hardcoded value 'lead'. An attacker can simply set x-ops-badge: lead to gain elevated access, bypassing the second authorization tier.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: The Django SECRET_KEY has a hardcoded fallback value 'unsafe-local-dev-key-change-me'. If the DJANGO_SECRET_KEY environment variable is not set in production, session tokens and CSRF tokens become predictable, enabling session hijacking and CSRF bypass.
